memo.verdict: A 15-unit to 16-unit mixed-use building is realistically achievable under an approved site plan valid through April 2027, but the project is not worth pursuing at the $475,000 asking price based on negative supportable land value projections.
memo.as_of_right: CD-5 zoning allows mixed-use multifamily as-of-right under Table 345.405.A-6. The 2,235 sq ft lot permits 100% coverage and 6 stories (approx 80 ft max height), yielding 13,410 gross sq ft. Deducting ground-floor retail leaves 11,175 gross residential sq ft, capping density at 15 to 16 units. Parking requires 1 space per unit plus 0.25 per bedroom over 1 under Table 345.405.N-1, with a 100% buyout option at $30,000 per space for small lots under Sec 345-405N(1)(h). Projects with 10 or more units require a 10% AFFH set-aside at 60% AMI under Sec 345-405.U.
memo.approval_path: Existing approval. The Planning Commission approved the site plan on April 25, 2022, and Local Law I-14 of 2025 extended approval through April 25, 2027. Time and entitlement risk are low if built as approved, but construction must vest before expiration.
legal_issues: Verification of approved site plan expiration date through April 25, 2027.
Unstated additional parking buyout and GEIS fair share mitigation fee amounts owed by the buyer.
Discrepancy in approved unit count between 15 units in Board of Trustees records and 16 units in AKRF review files.
Compliance with mandatory 50-year 10% AFFH affordable set-aside covenant at 60% AMI under Sec 345-405.U.
Floodplain compliance requirements and insurance costs due to FEMA Zone AE designation.
memo.test_fit: The building envelope is capped by a 2,235 sq ft footprint (100% coverage on 29 ft by 72 ft lot) and 6 stories. Total gross area is 13,410 sq ft, featuring 691 sq ft of ground-floor retail and 5 upper residential floors. The unit count ranges from 15 to 16 units (5 studios and 10-11 one-bedrooms). Tiny lot area and the 6-story height ceiling limit density first, not parking or FAR.
memo.value: Land cost at the $475,000 asking price is $31,667 per buildable unit for the 15-unit approved plan ($29,688 per unit if 16 units). A second analyst's pro forma estimates a maximum supportable land value of -$2,618,510 based on $450/sq ft hard costs and a 4.24% yield on cost, showing the ask exceeds supportable value.
diligence: Confirm site plan approval extension to April 25, 2027, in writing with the Village.
Clarify exact approved unit count (15 vs 16 units) from the stamped site plan set.
Obtain exact dollar figures for required parking buyout fees and GEIS fair share mitigation payments.
Verify building flood-proofing requirements and quotes for FEMA Zone AE flood insurance.
Confirm lot size of 2,235 sq ft and 29 ft frontage via a current boundary survey.
memo.enablers: CD-5 district as-of-right multifamily use, 100% lot coverage allowance, small-lot parking buyout up to 100% at $30,000 per space under Sec 345-405N(1)(h), and CD-5 Public Parking Incentive Zoning under Sec 345-405X.
memo.highest_and_best_use: Not enough data. FACTS lack verified local market rent comps, sale prices, and land comps (the second analyst relied on proxy rents from New Rochelle). Based strictly on zoning approvals, the highest density use is the approved 6-story mixed-use building with 15-16 apartments and ground-floor commercial.

memo.approval_path: As-of-right development. Standard and UAP multifamily developments require standard Department of Buildings plan examination without discretionary land-use approvals. Maximum building coverage is 40 percent (1,996 square feet) and maximum height is 42 feet or 3 stories, with no FAR limit specified. Setbacks require a 20 foot front yard, 15 feet total side yards, and a 25 foot rear yard. Off-street parking requires 2 spaces per dwelling unit, requiring 8 spaces for a 4-unit building.
memo.approval_path: The site requires Zoning Board of Appeals area variances or verification under Sec 267-13D for pre-existing lot eligibility because the lot area (4,991 sq ft) and width (50 ft) fall short of RMF-10 standards (10,000 sq ft and 75 ft). Pursuing ZBA variances adds entitlement risk and extends project timelines.

The seller sells the property as-is and makes no representations that the lot is legally buildable.
The listing advertises a two-family zone, whereas official city GIS records classify the parcel as RMF-10.

A 3-story massing yields approximately 5,827 gross square feet, which could physically hold 5 units at 1,150 gross square feet per unit. Density is limited first by the lot area per unit rule, capping development at 4 units. Required parking for 8 vehicles and driveways consume approximately 1,300 square feet, keeping total impervious coverage at 3,240 square feet, which complies with the 70 percent (3,494 sq ft) maximum limit.
memo.value: At the $269,000 asking price, land cost equals $67,250 per buildable unit for a 4-unit layout. At an estimated 60-foot frontage, the Double House A type allows 6 principal units plus 1 backyard cottage (7 total units) at 90 percent lot coverage and 2.5 stories. memo.verdict: A 19-unit to 28-unit multifamily rental building can realistically be built as of right, making the site worth pursuing at the $999,000 ask price.

This allows 17,200 gross square feet or approximately 19 units. Under UAP rules (ZR Chapter 27), FAR increases to 4.13 for 20,650 gross square feet or approximately 23 units. legal_issues: Existing two-family home is fully occupied and requires tenant relocation clear of lease obligations.
Discrepancy between listing lot size of 2,500 square feet and tax lot size of 5,000 square feet requires title confirmation.
Qualifying for the maximum 5.01 FAR requires executing a binding HPD or HDC regulatory agreement for permanent affordability.
memo.test_fit: The 50 by 100 foot lot yields a 3,500 square foot footprint after a 30 foot rear yard (ZR 23-342). The building envelope allows 7 stories at 75 feet standard height, or up to 10 stories at 105 feet under UAP rules. Expected unit count ranges from 19 standard units to 28 qualifying affordable units. Required parking is waived under ZR 25-232 because calculated demand is 6 spaces in the Outer Transit Zone. Floor area ratio caps density first.
memo.value: At the $999,000 ask price, land cost is $52,579 per unit for the 19-unit standard tier, $43,435 per unit for the 23-unit UAP tier, and $35,679 per unit for the 28-unit qualifying affordable tier. This compares well to local development comps, which traded from $89 to $168 per buildable square foot.

Tenant lease audit and rent roll review for the occupied two-family dwelling.
Title search to confirm ownership, legal description, and any open liens.
Phase I Environmental Site Assessment.
DOB property profile review to check open violations, permits, and occupancy records.
memo.enablers: City of Yes Universal Affordable Housing (UAP) bonus under ZR Chapter 27 and NYC HPD/HDC qualifying affordable programs allow FAR to expand from 3.44 to 5.01.

memo.approval_path: As-of-right development. This path carries minimal land-use approval risk and standard building permit processing timelines.
legal_issues: The listing address is NCNDA-gated and the parcel is not found in MapPLUTO records.
The deal is structured as a contract flip, requiring verification of assignability and original contract terms.
The 25-foot lot width presents structural design and zoning access challenges.
memo.test_fit: The lot envelope is 25 by 145 feet (3,625 SF). Total density permits 12,470 buildable SF, supporting 15 units at 795 SF or up to 18 units per broker listing. The narrow 25-foot width limits structural layout and floor plan efficiency first.
memo.value: At the $1,150,000 ask, land cost is $92.22 per buildable SF. This equals $76,667 per unit for a 15-unit scheme or $63,889 per unit for 18 units. This price sits below local comps ranging from $89 to $168 per buildable SF.
diligence: Confirm the exact tax lot and address missing from MapPLUTO.
Review the original purchase contract and assignment terms for the contract flip.
Verify R7-1 zoning controls and allowable floor area with the Department of Buildings.
Obtain a full title report and property survey.
memo.enablers: Bronx Metro-North Station Area Plan
memo.highest_and_best_use: Multifamily residential rental. New construction rental comps at The Bronx Vibe support rents of $2,580 for studios, $2,895 for 1-bedrooms, and $3,300 for 2-bedrooms. Condominium sale prices are not provided in FACTS.

memo.verdict: Realistically, a 4,952 buildable SF residential project or lot subdivision can be built, but pursuing it at the $649,999 asking price ($131.25 per buildable SF) is questionable without a price reduction given lower market comps.
memo.as_of_right: Under R4A zoning with a 1.0 FAR on a 4,952 SF lot, as-of-right development permits up to 4,952 buildable SF, allowing 6 units at an average size of 795 SF.
memo.approval_path: Development of the 4,952 buildable SF multi-family scheme is as-of-right with standard plan review, carrying low time and entitlement risk. Subdividing the lot or adding a second detached residence will require local site plan and lot split approvals.
legal_issues: Discrepancy between listing lot size (5,000 SF) and MapPLUTO lot size (4,952 SF, with parcel lot error in record).
Legal feasibility of lot subdivision and minimum lot frontage/width requirements for a second residence.
Unconfirmed occupancy status and existing single-family structure clear title.
Verification of listing details and zoning classification directly with the broker and municipal records.
memo.test_fit: The envelope allows up to 4,952 buildable SF based on 1.0 FAR. The site yields up to 6 units averaging 795 SF, or fewer units if developed as a subdivided lot with single/two-family homes. Density is limited first by the R4A 1.0 FAR cap.
memo.value: At the $649,999 ask, land cost is $131.25 per buildable SF ($108,333 per unit for a 6-unit build). This exceeds local land comps which range from $89 to $130 per buildable SF, such as 721 Saint Ouen Street ($120/buildable SF) and 4057 White Plains Road ($130/buildable SF).
diligence: Obtain an accurate property survey to confirm lot dimensions and resolve the 4,952 SF vs. 5,000 SF lot discrepancy.
Check municipal tax maps and MapPLUTO records to clarify parcel error.
Verify subdivision regulations and frontage requirements with NYC DOB/DCP.
Confirm listing details, property condition, and occupancy status with the broker.
Perform a full title search to inspect easements and covenants.
memo.enablers: The adopted Bronx Metro-North Station Area Plan (2024) introduces potential station area rezonings in surrounding neighborhoods (Parkchester/Van Nest, Morris Park, Hunts Point, Co-op City).
memo.highest_and_best_use: A multi-family rental building of up to 6 units (4,952 buildable SF) or a lot subdivision for an additional home is the highest and best use. Recent area rents reach $2,580 for studios, $2,895 for 1BRs, and $3,300 for 2BRs at The Bronx Vibe. Success depends on achieving a purchase price closer to market comps.

memo.approval_path: As-of-right development requiring DOB plan review and building permits without CPC or BSA approval, though mandatory MIH compliance and an HPD regulatory agreement are required for the affordable tier.
legal_issues: Mandatory Inclusionary Housing (MIH) area designation mandates a permanent affordable housing set-aside.
Environmental Designation E-848 requires environmental remediation approval from OER prior to building permits.
Commercial or manufacturing space in a mixed-use building is capped under ZR 123-62 / ZR 43-12 and reduces residential floor area.
memo.test_fit: The 7,711 sf lot has 88.64 ft frontage and 107.32 ft depth. Lot coverage caps the footprint at 80% (6,169 sf). Max height is 355 ft under MX rules, but density is limited by FAR first, permitting ~85 standard units or ~102 qualifying affordable units. No accessory residential parking is required in the Inner Transit Zone under ZR 25-21.
memo.value: The site is off market with no ask price. At an ask of zero, land cost per buildable unit is $0, but a second analyst's underwriting muse estimates negative maximum supportable land value (-$134,145 per unit for standard development) due to high construction costs relative to estimated yields.
diligence: Obtain OER requirements and scope of work for Environmental Designation E-848.
Review HPD MIH option requirements and regulatory agreement terms.
Commission a boundary survey to verify exact lot area, depth, and street width.
Obtain verified new-construction market rent and sale comps for the Astoria/LIC market area.

Under Universal Affordability Preference (UAP / ZR Chapter 27), qualifying affordable FAR increases to 7.20, generating 85,226 sf (approximately 94 units). Min lot area is 1,700 sf and min width is 18 ft (ZR 23-12). Maximum base height is 95 ft with a maximum building height of 125 ft for standard residential, expanding to 105 ft base and 145 ft total height for qualifying affordable housing (ZR 23-432, ZR 123-652(a)). Lot coverage is 80% for interior portions and up to 100% for corner portions (ZR 23-362).
memo.approval_path: As-of-right development path. Standard residential or qualifying UAP affordable construction requires only administrative plan examination and building permits from the NYC Department of Buildings without discretionary land use approvals.
legal_issues: UAP bonus floor area above FAR 6.02 requires an HPD/HDC regulatory agreement mandating permanent affordability at an average of 60% AMI or less, with at least 20% at 40% AMI or less.
Confirmation of absence of Mandatory Inclusionary Housing (MIH) requirements, as ZoLa verifies the parcel is in an Inclusionary Housing designated area rather than an MIH area.
Frontage on Gerard Avenue is labeled 60 feet wide (narrow street under ZR 12-10), requiring verification that contextual R8A bulk controls govern all building setbacks and envelope transitions.
Irregular lot geometry where frontage (214.38 ft) times depth (216.67 ft) exceeds the recorded 11,837 sf lot area, requiring boundary and lot area verification for final zoning calculations.
memo.test_fit: Standard envelope permits an 80% to 100% building footprint (up to 9,470 sf on interior portions) across approximately 11 stories (125 ft height limit) or 13 stories (145 ft limit under qualifying affordable). Total density is capped first by FAR (71,259 standard residential GSF or 85,226 qualifying affordable GSF), not by height or coverage. Likely unit range is 79 to 104 units standard, or approximately 94 units under the 7.20 FAR affordable scenario. Parking is located in the Outer Transit Zone under amended ZR 25-20 to 25-23 and does not restrict residential density.
memo.value: There is no asking price because the property is off market. Area land comps trade between $89 and $168 per buildable square foot ($60,417 per unit on Grand Avenue). The underwriting analyst estimates maximum supportable land value at -$21,571,486 for conventional rental and -$28,021,281 for affordable development, reflecting an analyst-assumed $0 offer price.
diligence: Obtain an architectural boundary and topographic survey to confirm exact lot area (recorded as 11,837 sf despite 214.38 ft by 216.67 ft dimensions).
Confirm with HPD the specific regulatory framework and agreement terms required to access the 7.20 FAR qualifying affordable tier under UAP.
Order an official title report and municipal search to verify ownership, easements, and absence of prior deed restrictions or transit easements.
Perform Phase I Environmental Site Assessment given the paired M1-4 industrial zoning and current Public Storage ownership.
memo.enablers: Universal Affordability Preference (UAP / ZR Chapter 27) and ZR 23-22 allow an increase in FAR from 6.02 to 7.20 and maximum height from 125 ft to 145 ft when utilizing qualifying affordable housing. The site also lies within the FRESH Zone and an Inclusionary Housing designated area.
memo.highest_and_best_use: Multifamily rental development is the primary viable use. Recent market rent comparables from The Bronx Vibe show studios at $2,580, 1-bedrooms at $2,895, and 2-bedrooms at $3,300. Whether market-rate rental (~79 units) or qualifying affordable rental (~94 units) maximizes value depends on construction pricing, real estate tax incentives such as 485-x, and the cost of capital.
memo.letter_angle: Approach Public Storage with an inquiry regarding surplus or non-core development rights on their Gerard Avenue parcel for a potential residential joint venture or outright acquisition.
